verdict.reasoning: Patient reports dizziness with room spinning, unsteady walking, and duration of about 2 hours: "my room is sort of spinning and I can't walk properly..." and later "it's there the whole time" and "So it's there now for the past two hours, you'd say?" / "Yeah."

Doctor confirms continuous symptoms for about 2 hours: "And is how long does it last for or is it there now? Continuously now?" Patient: "Yeah, it's there the whole time." Doctor: "So it's there now for the past two hours, you'd say?" Patient: "Yeah."
Patient explicitly describes vertigo as room spinning: "my room is sort of spinning" and in response to doctor: "Okay, so like the room spinning around?" Patient: "Yeah."

Patient reports difficulty walking straight related to vertigo: "I can't walk properly. Well, I can walk properly but not straight" and clarifies it is because "the room feels like it's moving a bit" and she feels "a bit unsteady."
Patient reports buzzing in ears: "my ears are buzzing a bit" and later: "It's just a bit of a buzzy noise in my ears." This is consistent with tinnitus.
Patient has nausea without vomiting: Doctor asks, "Have you been physically sick?" Patient: "No, but I am feeling very sick." Doctor: "Nausea."

Hearing is intact aside from buzzing: Doctor: "do you have any problems hearing at the moment? Like, is it muffled or something?" Patient: "It's just a bit of a buzzy noise in my ears, but otherwise I can hear everything."
Onset was sudden while making breakfast: Patient: "I was actually making my husband some breakfast and I... just suddenly felt very fuzzy and dizzy and a bit shaky."

Prior similar episode about a month ago lasting 5–10 minutes that resolved: Patient: "I had it a similar sort of thing about a month ago... it settled quite quickly" and later: Doctor: "How long did that episode last for?" Patient: "Probably only about five, ten minutes."

No recent URI: Doctor: "Did you have any kind of viral illness in the recent past. Past couple of weeks?" Patient: "No." Doctor: "No cold, cough, nothing?" Patient: "No, I've been pretty healthy, I think."
No ear pain or discharge: Doctor: "Any kind of ear pain or ear discharge, anything like that?" Patient: "No, nothing."
No fever reported: Doctor: "Do you have a temperature at all?" Patient: "I don't think so." This supports that fever is not present by history.
No limb weakness: Patient states, "my legs and arms and everything are working fine" and doctor reiterates, "So there's no weakness of your arms and legs?"
History of premature ovarian failure: Patient: "I've had premature ovarian failure and I've taken hrt." Doctor repeats: "HRT and premature ovarian failure."
Current hormone replacement therapy: Patient: "I've had premature ovarian failure and I've taken hrt." Doctor acknowledges: "HRT and premature ovarian failure."
No known allergies: Doctor: "Do you have any allergies at all?" Patient: "No."

Clinician assesses likely labyrinthitis with peripheral-vertigo features: Doctor: "the most common... diagnosis... is something called labyrinthitis" and notes treatment is a "middle ear sedative" for feeling "as if you're going around in a boat". History shows continuous vertigo for 2 hours, buzzing (tinnitus), nausea, and "my legs and arms and everything are working fine" indicating no focal weakness.
Clinician notes premature ovarian failure on HRT in PMH review: Patient: "I've had premature ovarian failure and I've taken hrt." Doctor: "Okay. HRT and premature ovarian failure."

Semitol dosing and food: Doctor: "It's called semitol. Yep. It's one tablet three times a day. So I'll give you about 10 days worth" and later: "It doesn't really matter. You can take it... might as well just take the tablets." This supports 3x/day for ~10 days and with or without food.

Prescription sent to Lloyd Pharmacy: Doctor: "So I'll send the prescription across to your pharmacy. It looks like it's the Lloyd Pharmacy on our system. Is that correct?" Patient: "Yeah." Doctor: "Yeah. So we'll send you across that prescription."

Plan for in-person review including otoscopy, BP, and gait/neuro: Doctor: "I would still like you to be seen by one of our doctors to take a look inside your ears" and later: "When... you're with the doctors, we'd like to do your blood pressure, just examine your, you know, you know, how you're walking, and everything is."

Safety-net advice for A&E: Doctor: "if you develop any weakness of your legs or arms or, you know, a sudden headache, any of those symptoms, or you start being violently sick with it, then, you know, you would need to take yourself to A and E." Persistent/violent vomiting is specified as "start being violently sick."
Instruction to call support to book appointment: Doctor: "Just make sure you call support to book that appointment. Okay?" Patient: "I will."
